title: The Integrity Test — An Unfolding Story
synopsis: A quarterly report overstates completion. You have hours to correct it while senior leadership pressures you to preserve a flattering headline.

opening.speaker: Dev Patel
opening.title: Ninety-Four or Eighty-One?
opening.text: Dev finds that unfinished cases were included in a 94% completion rate. The verified figure may be closer to 81%. “Please don't make this public,” Dev says.

choices.text: Pause release of the metric, preserve the source records, and ask Nina to verify the calculation.
choices.reaction: The record becomes more accurate while Dev and Nina can raise data quality concerns safely.
choices.coaching: Distinguish an honest error from intentional misconduct.

choices.text: Tell Dev you will fix the number later if anyone notices.
choices.reaction: An incomplete explanation leaves readers uncertain which figure they can rely on.
choices.coaching: A reassuring or incomplete answer may delay an uncomfortable issue, but does not remove responsibility.

choices.text: Keep the 94% because the underlying trend is still positive.
choices.reaction: The misleading statistic spreads and staff learn that appearance matters more than facts.
choices.coaching: Silencing evidence or substituting certainty for verification increases human and operational risk.

ending-strong.speaker: Narrator
ending-strong.title: Ending: Trust and Direction
ending-strong.text: The corrected report is delivered transparently. Dev receives fair review, and new validation controls reduce repeat errors.
ending-strong.reflection: Which observable behaviors made this result possible, and how will you repeat them?

ending-fragile.speaker: Narrator
ending-fragile.title: Ending: A Recoverable Gap
ending-fragile.text: The immediate record improves, but accountability and measurement standards still need documented follow-through.
ending-fragile.reflection: Which assumption or handoff would you revisit before the next decision?

ending-damaged.speaker: Narrator
ending-damaged.title: Ending: A Costly Leadership Pattern
ending-damaged.text: The overstated result informs decisions and the correction arrives late. Restoring credibility will require formal remediation.
ending-damaged.reflection: What would you acknowledge, repair and change first to prevent repetition?
